builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Fix Where It Fails: Root-Cause-Guided Agentic Harness Optimization for Scene Graph Generation
summary: RoHa-SGG replaces manual diagnosis and retraining of a failing model with LLM agents that analyze where and why a frozen model fails and then optimize the inference harness (prompting, post-processing, voting logic) around it. It costs LLM API calls for the root-cause analysis and harness search, added inference latency and complexity from the modified harness, and engineering effort to integrate the agent loop. It can fail if the diagnosed root causes do not transfer across datasets or model versions, if the searched harness overfits the evaluation split, or if API costs grow faster than the reported three-times-faster convergence implies.
rationale: The method requires only a frozen model plus LLM API access, which fits constrained infrastructure, but its gains are demonstrated only on scene graph generation and must be validated on the reader's actual workload before adoption.

claims.statement: RoHa-SGG replaces manual diagnosis and retraining of a failing model with LLM agents that analyze where and why a frozen model fails and then optimize the inference harness (prompting, post-processing, voting logic) around it. It costs LLM API calls for the root-cause analysis and harness search, added inference latency and complexity from the modified harness, and engineering effort to integrate the agent loop. It can fail if the diagnosed root causes do not transfer across datasets or model versions, if the searched harness overfits the evaluation split, or if API costs grow faster than the reported three-times-faster convergence implies.

Graph-constrained R@100 and mR@100 improve by up to 15.8 and 26.4 points for the multimodal LLM, and by up to 3.6 and 10.1 points for two-stage and one-stage models; root-cause guidance reaches the unguided search's final score up to three times faster.
